title: How we designed Shades of White — a warm minimal home in Gandhinagar
excerpt: A family wanted their new apartment to feel calm — not decorated. Here is how we translated that brief into one of our most cohesive interiors to date.
author: Blue Door Architects
body:
Every project begins with a brief. For Shades of White, the clients were a young family moving into a new apartment in Sargasan, Gandhinagar. They came to us with three words: calm, warm, and uncluttered.

Those three words became the entire design language.

The palette — cream, warm white, natural oak — was decided in the first week. We resolved never to introduce a colour that demanded attention. Everything would earn its place by texture and proportion, not by contrast.

The entry foyer sets the tone immediately. A sculpted Ganesha artwork in low relief sits above a fluted wood console — both monochromatic, both quiet. The moment you step in, the apartment tells you what kind of home this is going to be.

The living and dining areas flow openly, separated not by walls but by a black steel grid shelving unit. This became the spine of the apartment — a piece that defines zones while keeping the space connected. We designed it to hold objects the family already owned and loved, treating the shelving as a curated gallery rather than storage.

The Unikraft solid wood dining table was commissioned specifically for this project. White oak, with a subtle chamfered edge. It seats six comfortably and will last decades.

For the bedroom, we chose a panelled wall treatment in warm white — a classical reference executed in a completely contemporary way. Black swing-arm sconces provide reading light without clutter on the side tables.

The apartment was delivered in 11 weeks from first briefing to handover. Architecture, interiors, furniture — one team, one vision.
